objective: Players retain the existing game and saves while developers work on a supported, reproducibly installed Vue interface whose reactive updates and packaged startup are covered by browser tests.

include: Migrate the real application to a supported Vue 3 release, pinning exact dependencies during preparation and preserving static/local hosting.
Replace Vue 2 construction/global registration/reactivity APIs and affected template/event/lifecycle assumptions using the official migration guidance.
Serve/package the pinned runtime from the application artifact rather than fetching it from a runtime CDN; update real/test boot paths together.
Verify reactive game updates, save flows, keyboard interaction, layout and packaging against the existing browser baseline.
exclude: A new visual design, progression/balance changes, new accounts/backend services or save-format/key changes.
Paid Vue support, hosting changes, production deployment or mandatory purchase of tools/services.
Keeping Vue 2 and Vue 3 as parallel production modes, a permanent compatibility build, or test-only substitution that conceals the shipped dependency.

acceptance_criteria: UI01-AC01: Preparation inventories Vue 2 usage and affected templates/components, selects an exact supported Vue 3/runtime/toolchain combination from current official guidance and locks it. Document how the static/local artifact is produced and served without imposing a backend or changing hosting authority.

UI01-AC02: The shipped page uses Vue 3 application/component/lifecycle APIs and one canonical session owner. Vue.set and superseded Vue 2 boot/registration paths are removed; dynamic layer/upgrade arrays, save switching, tabs and derived-value changes remain visible through the actual reactive UI.

UI01-AC03: The built/served application includes its pinned Vue runtime and required game assets with attribution. A clean locked install produces the artifact, and startup works with the external Vue CDN blocked. Any remaining external fonts/assets are documented; this criterion is not a claim of universal offline/PWA support.

UI01-AC04: Browser fixtures cover fresh and representative early/middle/late saves, prestige/reset, purchase/automation, layer/tab selection, notifications, save/export/import/rename/select and error recovery. Values, controls, navigation context and valid saved progress match the behavioral baseline, with no unexpected console or migration warnings.

UI01-AC05: Rendered checks verify keyboard access/focus through changed controls, readable feedback, supported desktop and narrow layouts, and canvas/tree resizing after tab/window changes. Preserve existing interactions; record any unavailable accessibility/actual-user evidence without claiming synthetic tests prove usability.

UI01-AC06: Tests execute the same Vue version and boot path as the delivered artifact. Replace the TST01 Vue 2-specific local routing/fixtures where necessary, verify they cannot continue serving the old runtime, and run current rule/static/browser checks in CI against the integrated package.

UI01-AC07: Only one production UI runtime/boot path remains, with no permanent legacy fallback or dual state adapter. Existing save formats/key and Decimal semantics are unchanged; smoke-load recoverable baseline fixtures and document rollback to the prior code artifact without destructive data conversion.

UI01-AC08: The development guide identifies app/component owners, packaging/start/test commands, generated artifact sources and external dependencies. Record before/after representative startup/tick/render measurements for the same fixture and environment, without inventing a performance target or claiming improvement without data; publish an unmerged PR with known limits.
constraints: Planning/documentation only; no implementation, enrollment, merge or deployment authority
Follow AGENTS.md, current-main Orcha standards and existing lifecycle/permissions/writer controls
Preserve licenses, valid saves, layer IDs, save key and Decimal semantics
Hard dependencies require verified delivered source/tests and fresh exact-file preparation
No permanent legacy runtime modes, duplicate canonical models or silent failure fallback
No paid services, runner provisioning or account/policy changes

dependencies.reason: Its rendered journeys provide the behavioral baseline, including the current test-local Vue asset behavior.
Use the single explicit state and UI-command contracts after save/runtime/layer refactors.

decisions.question: Which bounded technical direction implements this review recommendation?
decisions.answer: Target supported Vue 3 while preserving the current static game, controls and canonical state contracts.
decisions.rationale: The owner requested milestones for the remaining review recommendations; official Vue guidance confirms Vue 2 is end of life. Exact compatible versions and packaging are bounded preparation choices, not a deployment grant.

owner_origin.request: Write milestones for the remaining work on the same branch.
owner_origin.scope: Remaining review-recommendation milestone documents on the existing PR #2 branch

standards.purpose: Fresh planning-run evidence; not a consumer pin

baseline: index.html currently loads Vue 2.6.12 from jsDelivr. components.js creates a Vue instance and registers global components; temp.js uses Vue.set. Vue 2 reached end of life on 2023-12-31, as confirmed by the official Vue notice. Existing template/global/reactivity assumptions must be inventoried before migration.
implementation_sequence: Refresh official Vue guidance and the post-DEV01 source, inventory breaking API/template/reactivity assumptions and capture representative browser evidence.
Migrate the application boot/components and dependency packaging in bounded increments, keeping tests on the same actual runtime and retaining compatible save data.
Remove old UI paths, run package/browser/static/regression checks and comparative measurements, then publish the unmerged migration PR.

verification_strategy.user_outcome: Players open an existing save, navigate layers/tabs, purchase/prestige, save/reload and recover from rejected import. Require rendered desktop/narrow and keyboard evidence, retained progress/context and source-matched runtime tests; actual-user usability remains a separately disclosed unknown.
verification_strategy.status: Planned; no application changes or implementation checks performed for this documentation request

risks: Vue proxy identity or template behavior can desynchronize the UI from game state; verify real visible updates after mutations and state replacement.
Test-only Vue routing can yield a green suite for a different runtime; verify artifact and test dependency identity.
A framework migration can grow into redesign; preserve controls, saves and hosting and surface consequential deviations before expanding scope.

documentation_assessment.organization: README links each canonical milestone; matching plan artifacts carry machine-readable evidence
strengths: Existing development guide and TST01 testing owner
defects: Current large/shared-state source owners make navigation and change verification harder; specific repairs stay with this milestone scope
documentation_assessment.improvement: Update the existing development guide alongside each implementation; do not add competing specifications or status ledgers
documentation_assessment.measurement: Qualitative source-backed assessment; no token/time savings claimed
